Name: Vending Machine
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: VENDING MACHINE

- This is a curious one. The Vending Machine is not so much a Hiss variant or even an "enemy" - as it is a corrupted piece of the decor of the Oldest House, now loose in the city.
- Note: the idea of a machine being corrupted doesn't quite fit our understanding of how the Hiss operate, so one could also argue that this outer appearance is just a clever disguise.
- The Vending Machine looks like a regular vintage piece of equipment until it is attacked, after which it flees. Is there any joy in this escape? Oddly, some reports suggest the chaotic pursuit is more thrilling than terrifying, almost like playing a game of tag with the Hiss rather than engaging in warfare.
- (And, even though the Vending Machine cannot be stunned nor executed as such, it can ultimately be destroyed.)
- Does this indicate some form of playfulness from the Hiss? I dare not even think what that might mean for us in the big picture - have we underestimated the Hiss and its functionality for years? Best to think of this specimen as an outlier.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Guard
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS GUARD

- This "Drone" enemy type has been observed attacking from a distance by using projectiles drawn from its surroundings, seemingly telekinetically.
- The Hiss Guard looks for higher ground, possibly to gain a clearer view of its opponent. This suggests some tactical thinking although "thinking" might not be the correct word to use regarding the Hiss.
- This enemy has better aim with a still target. Does this imply poor vision or poor coordination? Or is this Hiss variant simply impatient, hasty in its actions during combat?
- Note that if you get too close to the Hiss Guard, it will use a direct melee defense. Or attack, depending on your viewpoint.
- Relatively easy to defeat, especially in smaller numbers. Although, this statement is of course easy to make from the side-lines.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Charged
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS CHARGED

- Yet another known variant from the Hiss invasion that overtook the Oldest House.
- The Hiss Charged is a "Drone" enemy that boldly flies towards its target and, upon reaching it, self-detonates.
- This self-sacrificing method of attack has of course been used widely in ordinary human warfare as well. There, it carries a more tragic connotation, but in the context of the Hiss, it is merely an efficient means to an end.
- Due to its modus operandi, this enemy cannot be stunned. This Hiss variant also explodes upon death, making it a "living", flying landmine of sorts. Not pleasant.
- The damage the explosions cause is significant and affects the immediate surroundings, and sadly, we've seen it leave people with severe burns, in the cases where they live.
 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Elevated
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS ELEVATED

- This Hiss variant is familiar to us from the Oldest House invasion and seems to have remained in its original state even beyond the Lockdown.
- The Hiss Elevated is a "Drone" enemy that moves around by levitating, while appearing to keep the target in its line of sight.
- When airborne, the Hiss Elevated has been reported to deftly dodge some of our ranged attacks - a skill it has had plenty of time to practice.
- I've observed an interesting attack from the Hiss Elevated where it charges the target at considerable speed and hits them with a small impulse wave. Although this sudden attack momentarily drains the enemy, leaving it vulnerable on the ground, it still exhibits this behavior. A lack of strategical thinking or an "all or nothing" mentality? Can the Hiss exhibit either?

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Provoker
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS PROVOKER

- The Hiss Provoker is another "Drone" enemy that uses projectiles. but what makes this specimen especially interesting is its stationary nature.
- The enemy appears almost shy: it's encased within an armored shell to which it withdraws when its opponent comes near.
- However, with enough force, the protective shell can be destroyed, so this Hiss variant is not fully safe inside the little bubble it creates for itself. This begs the question is this an early phase of an evolution that would lead to a fully cocooned specimen? (Lydia, I'd like to hear your thoughts on this!)
- The casing itself seems to be the fleshy remains of the person this Hiss enemy used to be, and the operating part of it now only the skeleton. Disturbing.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Passenger
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS PASSENGER

- The Hiss Passenger, a fast and fairly small melee "Drone" enemy, seems to originate from the Hiss Transporter variant. This seems very logical, given their connection.
- The enemy's appearance is that of a passenger of the corrupted bus, fused together with their seat. Gruesome.
- I've observed this enemy using fast but simple melee attacks against its opponent when in close range. This methodology might indicate a specific "frustration" - perhaps due to the enemy being stuck to a chair, forever in transit, never arriving?
- This Hiss variant seems to lack tenacity, especially when separated, which is likely why they often fight in packs. Or crowds, like real passengers tend to do.
- Rangers who have encountered this enemy have stated that they were unable to stun the Hiss Passenger with their attacks, even when it was close to death.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Thug
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS THUG

- The Hiss Thug is a melee "Drone" enemy that exhibits slow movement as it advances on its target, then an equally slow melee attack when in range.
- To note, despite its apparent slowness, the Hiss Thug has been observed at times charging at the target and attempting an overhead attack. This move appears to happen when in medium range, possibly as an acute effort to overwhelm the opponent.
- This Hiss variant uses its elongated, misshapen arms as weapons. One might wonder is this intentional, opportunistic action or just a physical flailing, a symptom of the mutation?

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Transporter
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS TRANSPORTER

- The large origin of the Hiss Passenger, the Hiss Transporter is a "Heavy" enemy that appears to have formerly been a city bus, only now corrupted and hovering above the ground. A peculiar variant.
- This enemy is able to teleport when needed. Its motions are slow and almost avoidant as if this Hiss variant isn't so much interested in its opponent as it is in sending out its "spawn", the Hiss Passengers, to fight. An almost motherly dynamic.
- In a pinch, the Hiss Transporter will defend itself by slamming its large body to the ground, which creates a shock wave around it.
- I've observed our Rangers targeting the fused, former human bodies sticking out from the sides of the bus (an upsetting thing to see), and by destroying these parts of the enemy, being able to clearly weaken it.
- The above seems to indicate that the people inside the vehicle at the time of corruption are now all one, a part of the whole. While there is some strange beauty in this unity, it's clearly also able to destroy the one, the self. A common theme with the Hiss, I suppose.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Freighter
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS FREIGHTER

- The Hiss Freighter is a ranged "Heavy" enemy that, like the Hiss Collider, has an enlarged head but this variant is completely covered by armor.
- It appears this enemy's main attack is to launch arc projectiles from its head. This set-up is an unpleasant sight, especially if you suffer from trypophobia like I do. (A disadvantage in a job like this. Glad I'm not the only one dealing with this type of workplace hazard. If I'd known about your emetophobia, Lydia, you could've traded me some of your Mold assessments. Then again, maybe they wouldn't be much better for me?)
- I've observed Rangers managing to destroy the armor by dealing considerable damage to it, but also being attacked by a slow kick if they get too close. In a way, these fights have been quite equal on both sides.
- Frankly, I'm getting burned out on seeing all this violence and all these monstrosities. How many of these freaks of "nature" can there be?

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Collider
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS COLLIDER

- A melee "Heavy" enemy with a standout appearance; tall stature with a large and extremely deformed head.
- I've observed the Hiss Collider chasing its target quite slowly. then attacking them by slamming its head to the ground, using it almost like a large, fleshy mallet. It seems like this Hiss variant has little regard for its physical integrity as it uses its body/head brutally as a weapon.
- It appears that when in mid-range, the enemy rushes at the target, plowing them and anyone else in its path down with its head. It's horrific, but hard to look away.
- Gladly, I've witnessed some of our people being able to dodge or jump over the enemy when it is performing the above attack - much like a matador fighting a bull (a problematic "sport" but an apt comparison).

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Cluster
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS CLUSTER

- The Hiss Cluster is an enemy we're already familiar with from the Oldest House invasion.
- This Hiss variant is a "Heavy" type of enemy that does not participate in the battle directly, but appears to hide behind others and boost or even outright heal its nearby allies in the field.
- With its spherical shape and its very different mode of operating, this enemy certainly stands out from the rest. A medic of sorts, the Hiss Cluster enemies seem to be the supportive troops to the more direct aggressors. Interesting.
- Does the Hiss assign these different roles to individual Hiss variants according to some incomprehensible system or are they just born out of necessity there on the spot, like an improvised play? Your guess is as good as mine.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Distorted
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS DISTORTED

- Another familiar face from our seven-year battle against the Hiss.
- The Hiss Distorted is a "Heavy" enemy that is known to attack in close range with a conelike area of effect.
- It can become nearly invisible, and use this to its advantage, following its target while in this advantageous state. Then, when close enough, it attacks, after which it quickly retreats again. This is a cunning stealthy strategy. This enemy certainly doesn't lack any drive or patience. Maybe it's even enjoying this game of cat and mouse?
- I'd hate to be the mouse.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Riveter
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS RIVETER

- The Hiss Riveter is another ranged "Heavy" enemy.
- Its appearance reminds me of a deformed construction worker, complete with a jackhammer.
- This Hiss variant will throw said construction tool at its opponent when they're close to the ground. Mere seconds after this, the jackhammer's pressure spikes and it explodes, unable to contain the energy within. I've observed this explosion burning the people caught in it.
- The use of the tool as a weapon is interesting. Where other Hiss variants use themselves or their mutated body parts as weapons, this enemy carries a remnant of its former job and now uses it against others. There's some social commentary there - breaking free from the laborer's role, maybe?

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Ruiner
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS RUINER

- The Hiss Ruiner is a large, flying "Heavy" enemy with a somewhat ghost-like appearance (at least, to my wild imagination). It has holes in its chest from which it fires beams of energy in groups of three, using different combinations.
- I've discerned two other distinct attack styles with this Hiss variant. Both of these are more powerful than the above "simpler" attack, and will thus exhaust the enemy. One is what I call "Cruise" - the enemy flies over its target, firing explosive projectiles from its mouth, of all places. The other is what I call the "Dance" - the enemy fires all six of its energy beams at the same time while rotating around, almost like a rhythmic gymnast doing a pirouette with ribbons. While I might be making it sound elegant, it is a frightening sight.
- This Hiss variant appears to have a weak spot on its back. I've seen our people take this enemy down by utilizing said vulnerability during combat, as the Hiss Ruiner exposes it when exhausted.
- According to the Rangers' reports, the destruction of these weak spots takes three rounds to complete. Is three the magic number for any other Hiss variants? Something to look out for.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Pursuer
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS PURSUER

- Yet another melee "Heavy" enemy type.
- The Hiss Pursuer sports sharp arms that are shaped like huge scissors. Deeply unpleasant to see them in action.
- This Hiss variant appears to favor chasing its target at a fast speed, then using melee attacks when close enough to inflict harm.
- This enemy can also suddenly leap and land on an opponent from further away, with unfortunate consequences.
- Something about this variant's M.0. makes me think of a feral animal, hell-bent on the hunt. But perhaps I'm anthropomorphizing both animals and the Hiss with that imagery.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Focused
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS FOCUSED

- The Hiss Focused belongs to the ranged "Heavy" enemy group. This impressive variant uses a powerful beam of energy that tracks its target and pierces it upon contact.
- The relentless tracking reminds me of a sniper - you don't want to get caught in its crosshairs.
- I've observed this enemy being able to, quite nimbly. dodge some of our team's ranged attacks.
- The way the Hiss Focused operates - from a distance, with accuracy and relentlessness - makes me wonder why this method is not more favored among the Hiss. Maybe the evolution of the Hiss is a work in progress and the different variants are test cases, experiments? Or maybe it's all randomized, meaningless? I really don't know.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst. Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Transporter - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS TRANSPORTER - APEX

- One might think the Hiss Transporter does not require an "Apex" variant of itself, but alas, I've observed one in the field.
- This enemy variant appears to have expanded its use of its "progeny", the Hiss Passengers. It no longer just spawns them, but uses them as projectiles. (I take back my earlier note on the Hiss Transporter's motherly approach.) (And yes, Lydia, I know what you're going to say.)
- The Hiss Passengers that are used (and abused) in this manner fly straight at a target, hitting them impactfully, before resuming their regular chase behavior. At times, these makeshift projectiles even explode upon death. I'm not sure what to make of this change other than that the Hiss Transporter, and especially its "Apex" variant, seems to consider the Hiss Passengers completely expendable.
- Interestingly, there appears to be an additional weak spot, a destructible "extremity" on this variant. Is this the cost of the "upgrade" to its M.O.? Something to think about.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Freighter - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS FREIGHTER - APEX

- We have identified a powerful sub-type of some of the enemies to which we've given the moniker "Apex".
- The "Apex" variant of the Hiss Freighter appears to use the same attack methods the Hiss Collider and the Hiss Freighter variants use namely, the "head slam" and the "plowing rush" attack, and the launch of projectiles from its head.
- But from what I've observed about these more advanced variants, it seems like their attacks are notably enhanced. In this case, the "head slam" and "plowing rush" attacks are combined with challenging projectiles. Unfortunately, I have yet to see anyone survive.
- This improved efficiency may suggest we're seeing the Hiss evolve in real time. An unnerving observation.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Riveter - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS RIVETER - APEX

- The "Apex" variant of the Hiss Riveter seems to have upped its ante. Instead of throwing one jackhammer at its opponent, this enemy fires three of them at the same time. Efficient, yes. Challenging and deadly, also yes.
- As with the "baseline" variant of the Hiss Riveter, the jackhammers explode after hitting the ground, but now their order is randomized, making it even harder to avoid being in their blast radius. This feels cunning, almost devious but assigning morality to the Hiss is pretty much a dead issue.
- Subjective note: As someone who is not a fan of loud noises, this enemy is certainly not pleasant to observe in action.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Ruiner - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS RUINER - APEX

- The "Apex" variant of the Hiss Ruiner appears to have prolonged its "Cruise" attack. It now flies over its target and releases explosive projectiles three consecutive times instead of just the one. (Here it is again: "three" - this number seems to be tied to the Hiss Ruiner's behavior in the "Apex" form as well.) (Lydia, have you noticed this number come up in your assessments? Let's sync later!)
- I've observed this enemy's operating style, discerning how it differs from the "baseline" variant. It appears that when this enemy hits its opponents with either energy beams or projectiles, the victims are inflicted with the burn injuries that I've witnessed in other cases.
- The "Apex" enemy variants overall seem to be exceptionally dangerous foes to encounter. (Lydia, if they tell you I was at the Field Hospital, don't worry, it was just a couple burns. Could've been worse. Guess I should've taken your advice.)

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Distorted - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS DISTORTED - APEX

- The "Apex" variant of the Hiss Distorted has some subtle, but distinct "improvements" to its M.O.
- The conelike area of effect of its attacks is now expanded, and its attacks in general have a different rhythm; this variant attacks multiple times in a row between the states of invisibility it exhibits.
- This evolution in its behavior might suggest it's striving for a more effective offense, while preserving itself. It's unnerving to think about how much more the Hiss could evolve, given enough time.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Pursuer - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS PURSUER - APEX

- I got too close to this "Apex" Hiss variant while observing its attack patterns. The sickening twisting of its body and the sudden spinning, like a storm of sharp blades rushing at you... I was caught off guard.
- The Rangers present at the scene were able to intercept and pull me away, but they suffered burn injuries in the process. I'm very grateful for them.

 I could have died. Another close call like that and it might just be the end for me. I don't want to go without taking a chance on us, Lydia. Remember how we laughed at our ideal dates being the exact opposites of each other, how chaotic a pair we'd make? It doesn't have to be just a joke. I think we could have something real together, you and I. What do you think?

(Don't worry, you can tell me over coffee what a coward I am for not doing this in person.)

Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hiss Focused - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS FOCUSED - APEX

- The "Apex" variant of the Hiss Focused is able to become invisible at will, a skill previously only observed in the Hiss Distorted. Or rather, near invisible a very faint silhouette remains for the eagle-eyed (or those willing to get as close as I did) to see.
- This fits the "sniper-like" feel of the base variant that I remarked upon before, making this new skill the next evolutionary step for it.
- This enemy's energy beams appear to have evolved to be more destructive they now inflict the burning effect I've unfortunately witnessed with other types of Hiss as well. I suppose in a war like ours, you can't avoid getting burned.

 Rick Patel
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Host
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD HOST

- Classifying this as a "Drone"-type Mold variant
- Behavior: gets up close and personal; those big Mold clumps on its arms are used to clobber threats
- Regularly builds up and releases toxic spores around itself
- Spores are caustic; prolonged exposure causes severe lung damage and death
- Typically slow and ponderous in its movements
- Smells delicious (which I don't like to admit, but of all the Mold variants, this is the one I most want to take a bite out of, which skeeves me out but I can't deny it)
- Do not eat the Mold Host, obviously

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Launcher
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD LAUNCHER

- A "Drone" type Mold variant
- Lobs Mold projectiles at threats (we FBC types qualify as "threats," so keep moving!)
- Projectiles fragment upon impact and release what lay folks would call a "puddle of disgusting goo" (essentially, a liquid but equally lethal version of the caustic spores released by the Host variant)
- Prefers high ground when possible (follow up with the Research people: a sign of intelligence, or just that famous Mold adaptation at work?)
- Relatively fragile, but will put up a fight if anyone gets too close
- (Kind of like me in my first decade of relationships)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Spreader
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD SPREADER

- A resilient "Drone" type Mold variant
- Covered in hardened Mold growths in the front, but not in the back
- Produces spike-shaped, sharp Mold growths in its torso; launches them at nearby threats in a roughly cone-shaped pattern
- Takes a moment to charge up its spike launch attack!
- Completely lacks upper appendages (so at least it can't throw a punch)
- Instinctively (?) approaches and tracks threats, but moves slowly Kind of just... stumbles around and explodes barbs at people who get too close (possibly my mom at any family celebration)
- (I love you Mom but Jesus Christ)
- (I shouldn't leave these notes in but the world is ending, this is my outlet)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Spitter
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD SPITTER

- Another "Drone" type Mold variant
- Stationary (rooted?) when visible
- Can pull back into the ground, travel along an apparent hidden, rhizome-like Mold network, and reappear in another location
- Escapes if it senses a threat approaching
- Spits out spike-shaped Mold projectiles at anything it perceives as a threat
- Projectiles carry a potentially lethal Mold infection
- When killed (Destroyed? Is this stuff even properly alive?), leaves behind a toxic cloud

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Blight
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD BLIGHT

- A "Heavy" type Mold variant
- Similar in appearance/behavior to the "Scrapper"
- Like the Scrapper: packs a mean punch at close range, fast, highly aggressive
- Unlike the Scrapper: unarmored, doesn't jump, doesn't spew toxic Mold (however, see "geyser," below!)
- Biohazard! Its appendages are covered with infectious Mold; don't let this one touch you
- At distance, the Mold Blight can deploy what I have very officially codenamed a "geyser" attack: it plunges its upper appendages into the ground and, after a few seconds, showers of toxic liquid erupt from the ground around its target
- Note: bubbling on the ground is a visual indication of the impending "geyser"
- The exact mechanism of this is unknown, but my working theory is that it entices or instructs an underground network of Mold to build up and release the liquid either that, or it actually creates an underground channel and pumps the goop through it?
- (This is all speculation; if somebody wants to try and get an evaluation out of Underhill, be my guest, I can't deal with that. Rick? You've got more patience than me)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Scrapper
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD SCRAPPER

- To no one's surprise, classifying this big fella as "Heavy"
- Punches the hell out of anything it can reach
- Goes after threats (faster than you'd think!)
- Jumps like a flea - except you don't want it to land on you, or even near you, trust me
- Also spews out a stream of toxic Mold; this is then repeated twice in short succession (note that the Scrapper takes a few seconds to build up pressure!)
- The Scrapper's front is covered with hardened Mold growths, which can take a beating, so deploying proper maneuvers/ordnance might make a difference if it comes to a fight

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Disperser
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD DISPERSER

- A huge "Heavy" type, clearly an offshoot of the "Mold Plague" variant
- (I say "clearly" as if I knew which one of them came first; obviously I don't)
- Slow, ponderous
- Like the Mold Plague, the Mold Disperser has committed itself to being a truly disgusting abomination: if a threat gets too close, it vomits and vomits and vomits and vomits and vomits - Several tubelike structures on its back launch projectiles
- The projectiles inflate in midair and become balloon-like floating objects, which behave like aerial mines; they burst open and leave a toxic cloud
- The tubelike structures are a point of vulnerability: if destroyed, they cause the Mold Disperser to lose effectiveness (Stunned? Disoriented? Not sure either term applies to something like the Mold)


 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Plague
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD PLAGUE

- A huge "Heavy" type Mold variant
- Stomps around slowly
- Launches several Mold clump projectiles at threats from distance
- Upon impact, the projectiles burst open, resulting in caustic puddles of liquid Mold
- At close range, the Mold Plague exhibits truly gross behavior (trust me, you don't want to read the next sentence)
- If a threat gets too close, this nauseating blob of filth starts puking and pretty much doesn't stop: it just keeps coming and the puddle turns into a goddamn sea of lethal Mold vomit around it
- (Just typing this makes me want to take fifty showers)
- The Mold Plague's back carries a white Mold growth, apparently linked to something akin to a nervous system; reportedly, its destruction renders the Mold Plague much more vulnerable

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Spore Mother
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: SPORE MOTHER

- Falls under the "Heavy" category of Mold variants
- A huge floating Mold blob in a spheroid shape, consisting of Mold matter and, apparently, Mold-infected humans
- (Unclear what makes it float - some kind of lighter-than-air gas, paranatural field manipulation, what? needs further research) Can fire projectiles in any direction without turning
- Consistently fires two salvos of projectiles at targets (standard Mold projectile behavior: crack open, spread toxic goop, murder us)
- When the Spore Mother dies, it releases more projectiles that fall straight down, so don't get caught under it!
- (For the record, I was not the one who named this one "mother," that was Rick. I went to therapy and did the work precisely so I wouldn't feel the urge to do that)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Bloomed Spore Mother
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: BLOOMED SPORE MOTHER

- A resilient "Heavy" variant
- Huge floating lump that most field reports have described as "disgusting," and this assessor officially concurs
- "Minelayer"-type behavior: it excretes (ew) volatile lumps of Mold matter from its body and uses arm-like appendages to throw them
- Said Mold lumps stick to surfaces and detonate when a threat comes near (note the short delay between detection and detonation!)
- A crust (also ew) of hardened Mold essentially turns it into a floating tank

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Blight - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD BLIGHT APEX

- An "Apex" variant of the Mold Blight
- Unlike the normal Mold Blight, the Apex variant can leap around like its "cousin," the Scrapper
- When it lands, it causes "geysers" (pockets of high-pressure Mold liquid that spray up from the ground; see the baseline Mold Blight assessment for more disgusting details) to erupt around the landing site
- Notably hostile: when damaged, it deploys its "geysers" at a considerably more aggressive pace than the baseline variant
- Unfortunately, its aim also improves once it's angered; the "geysers" erupt directly under the target
- I say "angered," but there's no indication that the Mold in general, or this expression of the Mold in particular, has any emotional reaction to threats, or anything else, which I will admit does make me a little bit envious
- (Not to a degree where you need to report me to anybody, Ricky, you get worried way too easily. I'm okay, all things considered. Anyway, not all emotions are bad, some good ones sneak in too. especially when I beat you at chess. Want a rematch, by the way?)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Mold Plague - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD PLAGUE - APEX

- An "Apex" variant of the Mold Plague
- For baseline Mold Plague information, see the relevant assessment document (though I can't say I recommend it, don't say I didn't warn you)
- The Apex variant launches the Mold clump projectiles at a greatly increased rate
- In a bid to win the "most stomach-turning Mold construct" competition, the Apex not only produces vast quantities of vomit, it somehow also causes other, smaller Mold variants to grow out of said vomit
- As long as the Apex variant remains functional, combatants will also have to deal with increasing numbers of Mold "vomiants"
- I don't know what causes this to happen and I'm too nauseated to even consider looking into it (note to Research: ball's in your court, you deal with this. I can't)
- (It's a thing with me. I just can't, don't judge me)
- (I'm gonna go lie down)

 Lydia M.B. McPierce
Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team

Name: Hedron Spike
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SPIKE

- A "Drone"-class Hedron variant
- A Hedron-corrupted (coerced? co-opted? copied?) version of an Astral Spike
- (Background: Astral Spikes are believed to be native inhabitants of the Astral Plane; see ██████████ for more information)
- Native Astral Spikes are notoriously resistant to damage to the point of invulnerability: luckily, the Hedron Spike variant is much squishier
- The Hedron Spike attempts to approach targets; once close enough, dashes towards the target
- Visual identification is easy: if it looks like a migraine, you found one

Name: Hedron Base
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON BASE

- A "Drone"-class Hedron variant
- Essentially, a duplicate of the Hedron Flux variant, except some of its coordinates have been transposed
- Or to put it simply: whereas the Hedron Flux spins along its vertical axis, the Base variant spins along its horizontal axis
- Speculative documentation from Research indicates that all Base variants and all Flux variants may simply (and I use the word loosely) be literally the same individual that occupies multiple positions in space simultaneously

Name: Hedron Flux
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON FLUX

- A "Drone"-class Hedron variant
- Appears as a collection of smaller objects, fused (?) together into a shifting, recursive/geometric shape
- Capable of spatial displacement ("teleportation"); actively approaches threats
- At medium range, the Hedron Flux shifts its configuration into a vertical ring and advances towards the threat
- Upon reaching its target, the Hedron Flux shifts into a semicircle and performs repetitive spinning movements along its vertical axis
- According to Research, the identical objects that make up its body may, in fact, just be single instances of the object in question, occupying multiple positions in space simultaneously (...I'm not sure what to do with that information)

- Sudden rhythmic movements (possibly a part of larger pattern unclear)

Name: Hedron Sequence
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SEQUENCE

- Classification: Heavy
- Presents as a torus-shaped "swarm" of objects
- Maneuverable, defies gravity, attempts to maintain visual contact with threats
- ("Visual contact" is somewhat misleading given that they have no eyes and we have no idea how they sense anything - "line of sight" would probably be more accurate, but it's not like we even know that they have sight, so... ignore me)

- Classification: Heavy
- Visually resembles a brick wall pulled together into a toroid-like shape
- Flight-capable in a way bricks really aren't supposed to be; charges rapidly at threats
- Releases a wave of "force" (field reports are as of yet inconclusive; tentatively a wave of kinetic energy?) at the end of the charge

Name: Hedron Axiom - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AXIOM - APEX

-"Apex"-class Hedron variant, evidently based on (or a fork of?) both the Aggregate Apex and Axiom variants?
- As usual, invulnerable to direct assault
- Follows a three-state behavioral pattern as it takes damage:
- STATE 1
- Flux and Base variants surround the Apex; damage to them is reflected onto the Apex itself
- Fires a beam at one of the Flux/Base variants (chosen at random?), which is then refracted into multiple beams
 - STATE 2
- The Apex becomes passive temporarily
- The Flux/Base variants detach and commence firing bidirectional beams
- The smaller variants soon return to the Apex, and a new, more aggressive cycle of attacks begins
 - STATE 3
- Flux/Base variants again detach and fire independently at threats
- However, the Axiom Apex itself now starts launching "energy discs" (best name I've got, sorry)
- Once enough Flux/Base variants are destroyed, the Axiom Apex becomes faltered

Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AGGREGATE - APEX

- Hooo boy, where to even start with this one! Intel's spotty: as is often the case, much of this comes from interviews with Dylan Faden (see ██████████)
- An "Apex" version of the Hedron Aggregate variant?
- Unaffected by gravity, immobile, impervious to direct harm
- Because nothing can ever be simple, this thing operates in three states:

- Launches great numbers of projectiles in specific patterns (rows, columns, diamonds)
- Surrounded by Flux and Base variants in "satellite formation"
- Damage to the Flux and Base variants is reflected on (passed on to?) the Aggregate Apex itself
- STATE 2
- Once the variant suffers enough damage, it becomes passive. and the Flux/Base variants detach and pursue threats
- They soon return to the Aggregate Apex, and a new, more complex cycle of movement and projectiles begins
 - STATE 3
- Flux/Base variants again detach and pursue target
- Aggregate Apex itself now remains active and continues to send out projectiles
- Once enough Flux/Base variants are destroyed, the Apex becomes faltered

Name: Hedron Sequence - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SEQUENCE - APEX

- The Hedron Sequence "Apex" is a Hedron variant consisting of swarms of normal Hedron Sequence variants
- As other Hedron Apex variants, it is invulnerable to direct assault, and it follows a three-state behavior pattern
- Consists of two distinct groups of Hedron Sequence variants: the "core" group and the "satellite" group
- STATE 1
- The satellite group detaches from the core and flies out to attack threats with homing projectiles
- The core group suffers damage when the satellite group is attacked
 - STATE 2
- After enough damage has been inflicted, the core recalls the satellites, and attacks by manifesting (teleporting?) small, exploding objects near the target
- The core also manifests Flux variants
- Resumes its prior behavior, albeit much more aggressively
 - STATE 3
- After suffering more damage, again behaves as above, except threats appear at an increased rate
- Once enough satellites have been destroyed, the Sequence Apex becomes faltered
- (Hey Ricky, this is out of left field, but if we actually survive this, wanna grab a coffee sometime?)

Name: Hedron Vector - Apex
Description:
THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON VECTOR - APEX

- Another "Apex"-class variant built out of swarms of Vector variants
- Invulnerable to direct assault, three states of behavior
- Has two elements: a "core" group and a "satellite" group, both made up of Hedron Vector variants.
- STATE 1
- At regular intervals, the satellite group detaches and makes independent attack runs
- Any damage suffered by the satellite group is reflected onto the core group
 - STATE 2
- Once the core is damaged enough, the satellites spread out and periodically initiate a "black hole" sequence, pulling threats in, causing injury via an "impulse wave"
- Returns to its previous routine, albeit with more aggression and more "black hole" activations
- (Side note: Research is debating if the "black hole" effect is an actual black hole. Disturbing that it's even a question)
 - STATE 3
- After further core damage, the satellites separate and engage in intense "black hole" activity as before, but now the core also releases Flux variants
- At this stage, the Apex can be made to falter by destroying enough of the satellite units
